name: Slavoj Žižek
summary: Slavoj Žižek is a Slovenian philosopher and cultural critic who writes on Hegel, Lacan and Marx, calls himself a communist, criticises both nationalist populism and liberal moralism over migration, and argues for a new universalism and a communist response to ecological and global crises.

sources.title: The Non-Existence of Norway, London Review of Books (9 September 2015)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: The refugee crisis: open-border advocates as hypocrites, an all-European plan, global capitalism and communism reinvented.

sources.title: We Can't Address the EU Refugee Crisis Without Confronting Global Capitalism, In These Times (2015)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Refugees must respect European laws and norms; ethical universalism against both anti-immigrant brutality and uncritical tolerance.

sources.title: 'Piss Christ', Internationalism, and the Night of the World: Interview with Slavoj Žižek (Philosophy World Democracy)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek, Kamran Baradaran and Anthony Ballas
sources.usedFor: Nationalism has no global emancipatory potential; the moralist left and open borders; China.

sources.title: After Trump's Victory: From MAGA to MEGA, e-flux Notes (November 2024)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Communism needed more than ever for ecology, war and AI; the left must distance itself from the liberal centre and its 'woke corporatism'.

sources.title: Which Idea of Europe is Worth Defending?, Crisis and Critique 7(1)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Europe against Trump and Putin; left populism's national sovereignty; universal solidarity.

sources.title: 'What I don't want is Western triumphalism': Slavoj Žižek on Putin's expansionism, Western complicity..., Meduza (3 February 2023)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Ukraine, the EU needing more cooperative centralisation, democracy and the Yeltsin years.

sources.title: Interview with Slavoj Žižek, Philosophy Now issue 122
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Why communism: the commons; the era of the nation state is over; capitalism is falling apart yet most dynamic; ecology.

sources.title: The Prospects of Radical Change Today, tripleC 16(1) (2018)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Lenin's State and Revolution and Stalinism; the revolutionary subject; elections and the people; class struggle and immigration; human rights as basic material rights; Europe's emancipatory core.

sources.title: In the Wake of Paris Attacks the Left Must Embrace Its Radical Western Roots, In These Times (16 November 2015)
sources.author: Slavoj Žižek
sources.usedFor: Minimum norms for all (religious freedom, individual freedom against group pressure, women's rights), limits on free movement, gay and women's rights, class struggle and global solidarity.

tried.how: only reviews and excerpts turned up; no open full text

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He called pacifism in the face of the Russian attack on Ukraine a version of 'imagine' and argued that Europe must wake up to the need for a stronger NATO.

abortion-legal.rationale: He wrote that Europe is fighting for women's rights including the right to abortion and that these rights should not be dismissed as marginal when refugee customs conflict with them.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: He demanded obligatory norms including religious freedom and protection of individual freedom against group pressure, within which different ways of life are tolerated.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: He said that capitalism, at least as we know it, is approaching an end, citing ecology, fictional capital and refugees, and that capitalism is falling apart.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He said that though a good Marxist he is not altogether against capitalism because it is the most dynamic system in the history of humanity.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He insisted that norms of religious freedom, individual freedom and women's rights be upheld without fear of seeming Eurocentric, and wrote that the European emancipatory legacy should not be equated with cultural imperialism and racism.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: He endorsed the view that human rights are first of all basic material rights, 'toilets, kitchen, healthcare', which come before free speech and other higher rights.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He wrote that in elections the 'people' are reduced to a mechanical collection of individuals and that the basic political problem today is how best to reconfigure democracy, not merely hold elections.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He said that taxes and regulation cannot do enough about ecology and that a big catastrophe needs larger actions.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: In June 2022 he argued for a stronger NATO, saying pacifists cling to a world of 'imagine'.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He wrote that Europe's identity is not threatened by refugees but by anti-immigrant populists such as Le Pen and Wilders, who are the true threat to the Enlightenment's emancipatory core.

leader-cult.rationale: He criticised the 'totalitarian Party and its Leader' as a direct embodiment of the People and the Stalinist and Maoist tradition of endorsing brutality with no constraints.

material-over-identity.rationale: He wrote that the left should clearly distinguish itself from the 'progressive' liberal centre and its 'woke corporatism' and called for communism as the way to confront ecology, war and AI.

nation-first.rationale: He said that the era of the nation state, where the highest ethical value is readiness to sacrifice yourself for your country, is over and that we need larger transnational forms of coordination, and that nationalism has no global emancipatory potential.

one-party-rule.rationale: He called it the mistake of 'totalitarianism' to claim that the people exists through a determinate agent, the totalitarian Party and its Leader, which acts as if it directly embodies the People's true Will.

open-borders.rationale: He wrote that the right to 'free movement' should be limited and that the greatest hypocrites are those who call for open borders, which would instantly trigger a populist revolt in Europe.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He praised political assemblages on public squares in which the inert mass of ordinary people is transubstantiated into a politically engaged united force.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He said the EU needs more cooperative centralisation to confront ecological crises, immigration and the war, and defended Europe's emancipatory idea against Trump and Putin.

public-ownership.rationale: He said communism is the name of the problem of the commons, shared substance such as ecology, intellectual property and biogenetics that should not be privatised and left to the market.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He wrote that it is today's anti-immigrant populists who are the true threat to the emancipatory core of the European Enlightenment and that a Europe ruled by Le Pen or Wilders is no longer Europe.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: He wrote that if a woman chooses to cover her face her choice should be respected, while insisting that her freedom not to cover it be guaranteed.

sacred-nation.rationale: He wrote that every authentic leftist should ferociously oppose the claim that treason, the betrayal of one's own nation-state, is the gravest crime, since there are circumstances when treason is the greatest act of ethical fidelity.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He wrote that Europe is now fighting for full gay and women's rights, including the rights of same-sex married couples, and asked whether these rights should extend to gays and women among the refugees even against the customs they bring.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: In June 2022 he wrote that the least we owe Ukraine is full support and that to do this we need a stronger NATO, calling pacifism the wrong response.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: He called for a minimum set of norms obligatory for everyone, including religious freedom, protection of individual freedom against group pressure and the rights of women, enforced by the force of law if communication fails, without fear that they seem Eurocentric.

universal-morality.rationale: He argued that a defence of one's own way of life does not exclude ethical universalism and that the cure for populism is a new universalism.

workers-nation.rationale: He wrote 'let's bring class struggle back — and the only way to do it is to insist on global solidarity of the exploited'.

notes: First audit. Read in full: his LRB essay on the refugee crisis (2015), In These Times piece, the RT interview, an interview in Philosophy World Democracy, an e-flux essay of 2024, a Crisis and Critique paper on Europe, and the Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy entry. His essays use provocation and irony, so only passages stating a position are used. Searched without a settled answer: capitalism and planning, democracy, revolution and violence, religion, gender, the state, ecology and climate, nationalism and populism. The tripleC interview (Ben Gook, 2020) and a Meduza interview (2023) were also read; Project Syndicate columns are open only as excerpts ('register to continue') and are not used; the Peterson debate has no open full transcript; the Philosophical Salon pages found are commentary by others, not his own text; the Conversations with Tyler transcript refused automated access (403) and was not retried. Nothing read gives a position on most statements; they stay null. YouTube and MediaSum hold no transcripts of him (MediaSum: none).
